children.text: ambhodhiḥ sthalatāṃ sthalaṃ jaladhitāṃ dhūler lavaṃ śailatām
children.translated_text: The ocean becomes dry land, and dry land becomes ocean; a speck of dust becomes a mountain,

children.text: śailo mṛtkaṇatāṃ tṛṇaṃ dahanatāṃ vajraṃ tṛṇakṣīṇatām
children.translated_text: a mountain becomes a particle of clay; grass becomes fire, and a thunderbolt is reduced to the weakness of grass,

children.text: vahniḥ śītalatāṃ himaṃ dahanatām āyāti yasyecchayā
children.translated_text: fire becomes coolness and snow becomes fire, by whose will this comes to pass:

children.text: līlānāṭyakṛte bhuvo bhagavate kṛṣṇāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ
children.translated_text: to you, blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, maker of the play-drama of the earth, homage.
I worship <s>Rāma</s>, dark like a fresh rain-cloud, clothed in yellow silk, the delight of <s>Videhajā</s>,
shining with a garland bearing the <s>Kaustubha</s>, an embodiment of auspiciousness.
Health is said to be the root of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, pleasure, and liberation.
Therefore engagement in the science approved by good physicians is proper.
Having carefully considered, from beginning to end, the works of <s>Mādhavakara</s>, the well-ordered Ocean of Treatment,

children.text: pathyāpathyam atho vipākam akhilaṃ tāvan nṛṇāṃ karmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the wholesome and unwholesome regimen, digestion, and the whole extent of men's actions,
and the complete countermeasures known from works like the great ocean, now,
because of fear of excessive prolixity and the like, a newer <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> is being set forth.
Abandoning the sequence of the immediately manifest symptoms of <s>Mādhava</s>, for the sake of quick understanding,

children.text: gadasya sāmānyaviśeṣatattvair yuktāni kurve kati lakṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: I compose some symptoms of disease, joined with the principles of their general and particular features.

children.text: śabdārthāvagame bhajanti sakalā devā sadā mūkatāṃ manye kiṃtu viśanti pāram paraṃ duṣpāraśāstrāmbudheḥ
children.translated_text: In understanding word and meaning, I think all the gods always become mute; yet they reach the further shore of the hard-to-cross ocean of śāstra.

children.text: kartuṃ yady api śakyate laghutayā sāraś cikitsārṇavo doṣo jātu bhaviṣyatīti manasā nyūnādhiko na kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although the essence of the Ocean of Treatment can be made brief, thinking that some fault might arise, I have not made it deficient or excessive.

children.text: cintāmaṇeḥ prathamataḥ kiraṇaiś caturbhiḥ dravyasya mānam akhilasya rasasya śuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: First, by the four rays of the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, there is the measure of every substance and the purification of rasa,

children.text: kālāditattvakathanaṃ tv atha nāḍikādes tattvaṃ tato 'nyakiraṇair upacāraṇāya ||
children.translated_text: then the exposition of the principles beginning with time, and thereafter, by the other rays, the principle of the pulse and so on, for treatment.

children.text: śāstreṣu śramavān kriyāsu kuśalaḥ prājñaḥ sudhīḥ satyavāk dhīro roganirūpaṇaikakuśalaḥ pīyūṣahastaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: A physician is one who is diligent in the śāstras, skilled in procedures, wise, intelligent, truthful in speech, steady, uniquely skilled in determining disease, nectar-handed, pure,

children.text: dravyāṇāṃ rasavīryakāryam akhilaṃ jñātā dayāluḥ sadā nirṇetā ṛtukāladeśavayasāṃ mātrādhikārī bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: knowing fully the taste, potency, and action of substances, always compassionate, able to decide season, time, place, and age, and competent in dosage.
A rasa-physician is divine; one using roots and the like is human.
One rich in cutting instruments and cautery is demonic, while a perfected physician is one skilled in mantra.
Those known for herbs are inferior, and those known for decoctions are middling.
Those called excellent are rasa-physicians: such is the threefold determination of physicians.
He whose feet are marked with lotus and goad, and whose hands bear the auspicious signs of fish and bow,
and whose lines are red and sprouting, that physician is nectar-handed.
He who at the outset is fond of boasting, attached, greedy, and without a teacher,

children.text: kṛṣṇarekhāṅkuro yas tu dagdhahastaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and whose lines are black and sprouting, is called burnt-handed.

children.text: avijñāya tu śāstrārthaṃ prayogaṃ kārayed bhiṣak
children.translated_text: But a physician who carries out treatment without knowing the meaning of the śāstra
should be known as equal to <s>Yama</s>, assuming the form of death for mortals.

children.text: vinā śāstro yo brūyāt tam āhuḥ brahmaghātakaḥ
children.translated_text: One who speaks without śāstra is called a killer of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: naro narakapātī syāt tasya sambhāṣaṇād api ||
children.translated_text: A man would fall into hell even from conversing with him.

children.text: na jānāti ca śāstrāṇi lakṣaṇaṃ yo na vidyate
children.translated_text: And the one who does not know the śāstras and does not understand the symptoms

children.text: mārayaty āśu jantūnāṃ sa vaidyo yamakiṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly kills living beings; that physician is an attendant of <s>Yama</s>.
One who is lame, hunchbacked, crooked, with a deformed head, with the ear extending to the pulse-line,

children.text: eko netra rujāvabhakṣitatanu kṛṣṭī bhavet ślīpadī ||
children.translated_text: one-eyed, with a body consumed by disease, afflicted with skin disease or elephantiasis,
devoid of <s>Āyurveda</s>, tawny in form, or attached like a madman to women,

children.text: vaidyaṃ rasam auṣadham anahitaṃ rogī akāle mriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such a physician, rasa, or medicine is unsuitable; the patient dies at the wrong time.
Complete knowledge of the disease's reality and the restraint of pain:

children.text: etad vaidyasya vaidyatvaṃ na vaidyaḥ prabhur āyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is the physician's physicianhood; the physician is not the lord of life-span.

children.text: kucelaḥ karkaśo lubdhaḥ kugrāmī svayam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Badly dressed, harsh, greedy, from a bad village, or come on his own initiative:

children.text: pañca vaidyā na pūjyante dhanvantarisamā yadi ||
children.translated_text: these five physicians are not to be honored, even if they are equal to <s>Dhanvantari</s>.

children.text: na mānena vinā yuktir dravyāṇāṃ jāyate kvacit
children.translated_text: Without measure, no proper application of substances ever arises.
Therefore, for the success of preparations, the <s>Māgadha</s> measure is stated.
What is seen in a beam of the fierce sun passing through a lattice is called a dust-mote,

children.text: tataḥ prāhus trasareṇu tatra ṣaḍbhir ājāhvayā sarṣapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from that, they say, six make the mustard seed called <s>ājā</s>.

children.text: syād ebhis tribhir eva toḍitatanu gaurāhvayaḥ sarṣapaḥ ṣaḍbhis taiś ca yavo bhaved atha yavair etais tribhī raktikā
children.translated_text: With three of these there is the pale mustard seed called <s>gaura</s>; with six of those there is a barleycorn, and with three such barleycorns a <s>raktikā</s>.

children.text: guñjaḥ syāt triyavaiś ca raktiyugalaṃ vallaś ca tatpañcakair māṣomāṣacatuṣṭyam nigaditaṃ śāṇaś ca śānadvayam ||
children.translated_text: A <s>guñjā</s> is three barleycorns; two <s>raktikā</s>s make a <s>valla</s>; five of those make a <s>māṣa</s>, and four <s>māṣa</s>s are stated to make a <s>śāṇa</s>, with two <s>śāṇa</s>s next.

children.text: kolaṃ draṃkṣaṇakaṃ tathaiva vaṭakaṃ koladvayaṃ karṣakaṃ cākṣaḥ pāṇitalaṃ viḍālapadakaṃ tadvat suvarṇaṃ picuḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>kola</s>, a <s>draṃkṣaṇaka</s>, likewise a <s>vaṭaka</s>; two <s>kola</s>s make a <s>karṣaka</s>, also called <s>akṣa</s>, <s>pāṇitala</s>, <s>viḍālapadaka</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>, and <s>picu</s>.

children.text: karṣābhyām api śuktikā nigaditā karṣaiś caturbhiḥ palam bilvaṃ muṣṭir athāpi śuktiyugalaṃ syāt kuñcikā ṣoḍaśī ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>karṣa</s>s are stated to make a <s>śuktikā</s>; four <s>karṣa</s>s make a <s>pala</s>. A <s>bilva</s> or fistful is also a pair of <s>śukti</s>s, and a sixteenth part is a <s>kuñcikā</s>.

children.text: bilve dve 'pi mānika ca prasṛtaṃ nāmnā caturbhiḥ palaiḥ yuktaḥ syāt kuḍavo 'ñjaliś ca palikāny aṣṭau śarāvo bhavet
children.translated_text: Two <s>bilva</s>s are also a <s>mānika</s>, and by name a <s>prasṛta</s>; with four <s>pala</s>s there is a <s>kuḍava</s>, and an <s>añjali</s>; eight <s>palikā</s>s make a <s>śarāva</s>.

children.text: tanmānaṃ dharaṇaṃ palasya daśamo bhāgo bhavet yatsthitaṃ vidyāc cāpi śataṃ palāni ca tulā bhāras tulāviṃśatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its measure is a <s>dharaṇa</s>; the tenth part of a <s>pala</s> should be known as what is fixed there; and one hundred <s>pala</s>s are a <s>tulā</s>, while a <s>bhāra</s> is twenty <s>tulā</s>s.

children.text: prasthaḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ palair atha catuḥ prasthaṃ bhaved āḍhakaṃ kaṃsaḥ pātram athāḍhakāni ca punaś catvāri saṃjāyate
children.translated_text: A <s>prastha</s> consists of sixteen <s>pala</s>s; four <s>prastha</s>s make an <s>āḍhaka</s>; a <s>kaṃsa</s> is a vessel, and again four <s>āḍhaka</s>s come into being.

children.text: droṇoralvaṇavyarmaṇaṃ ca kalaśo droṇadvayaṃ syāt punaḥ sūrpaḥ kumbham ihollikhanti ca catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ śarābā śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>droṇa</s>, and further a <s>kalaśa</s> is two <s>droṇa</s>s; here they also record a <s>sūrpa</s>, a <s>kumbha</s>, and sixty-four auspicious <s>śarāva</s>s.

children.text: droṇī droṇacatuṣṭayena tulikā tasyāḥ śarāvāḥ śatam aṣṭaviṃśatisaṃyutaṃ ca bharikā syur mānasaṃpratyaye
children.translated_text: A <s>droṇī</s> is by four <s>droṇa</s>s; a <s>tulikā</s> consists of one hundred and twenty-eight <s>śarāva</s>s, and a <s>bharikā</s> is so in the convention of measures.

children.text: māṣaḥ śāṇapicuḥ palaṃ ca kuḍavaḥ prasthas tathā cāḍhako droṇo goṇyapitāś caturguṇatayā nirdhāritāḥ syuḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: A <s>māṣa</s>, <s>śāṇa</s>, <s>picu</s>, <s>pala</s>, <s>kuḍava</s>, <s>prastha</s>, <s>āḍhaka</s>, <s>droṇa</s>, <s>goṇī</s>, and <s>pitā</s> are fixed successively by being fourfold.

children.text: yavaḥ syāt sarṣapaiḥ ṣaḍbhir guñjā tu syāt tribhir yavaiḥ
children.translated_text: A barley grain is made of six mustard seeds, and a <s>guñjā</s> is made of three barley grains.
One <s>māṣaka</s> is said to consist of five <s>guñjā</s>s.

children.text: bhavet ṣoḍaśabhir māṣaiḥ suvarṇas tat punaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>suvarṇa</s> consists of sixteen <s>māṣa</s>s; that again is remembered as such.

children.text: caturbhiḥ palam etasya daśamo dharaṇo viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know a <s>pala</s> to consist of four of these, and a <s>dharaṇa</s> to be its tenth part.
Ten <s>pala</s>s are a <s>dharaṇa</s>; four <s>suvarṇa</s>s are a <s>niṣka</s>.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ navīnaṃ sakaleṣu yojyam dravyaṃ tathārdraṃ dviguṇaṃ prayojyam
children.translated_text: In all cases a dry or fresh substance is to be used as prescribed, and a moist substance is to be used in double quantity.

children.text: śuṣkasya tāvad guru tīkṣṇasattvāt tadarddhabhāgaḥ parikalpanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since a dry substance is heavy to that extent because of its sharp potency, half of that quantity is to be calculated.
Beginning with the measure of a <s>guñjā</s> and so on up to the state of a <s>kuḍava</s>,
the measure of liquid, moist, and dry substances is considered the same up to that point.
Beginning with the measure of a <s>prastha</s>, however, that measure is doubled for liquids and moist substances.
Even with a <s>kuḍava</s> there is doubling in some cases, as is remembered in the case of <s>dantīghṛta</s>.

children.text: palaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ prasthaḥ śuṣkāṇāṃ ca tato viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know a <s>prastha</s> of dry substances to consist of sixteen <s>pala</s>s.
For fresh juices and moist substances, and for substances like oil, milk, and molasses, it is double.
Moreover, parched grain, milk-rice, coconut water, urine, water, and sour gruel,

children.text: dvātriṃśatpalakaṃ tadarddham uditaṃ prasthaṃ rasaṃ cauṣadham ||
children.translated_text: are said to be thirty-two <s>pala</s>s; half of that is stated to be a <s>prastha</s> for medicinal juice.

children.text: kṣaudraṃ tailaghṛte ca viṃśatipalaṃ kṣīrasya triṃśatpalam
children.translated_text: Honey, oil, and ghee are twenty <s>pala</s>s; milk is thirty <s>pala</s>s.
Curds are twenty-five <s>pala</s>s, and molasses is said to be seventeen <s>pala</s>s.
Some say that, for iron, clay, and stone, a <s>prastha</s> consists of twelve <s>pala</s>s,
and also for alkali, mercury, musk, camphor, and substances born in Kashmir.
In these varieties of <s>prastha</s>, one <s>pala</s> consists of sixteen <s>niṣka</s>s.

children.text: mūlatvak dārupattrāṇāṃ puṣpasya ca phalasya ca
children.translated_text: For roots, bark, wood, leaves, flowers, and fruits,
and for rock-salt, clay, clods, metals, and cow dung,
a <s>prastha</s> is sixteen <s>pala</s>s; lac, camphor, and guggulu
make a <s>prastha</s> of twenty-one <s>pala</s>s. This is the definition of a <s>prastha</s>.
In all procedures, all substances are to be used fresh,

children.text: vinā viḍaṅgakṛṣṇābhyāṃ guḍadhānyājyamakṣikaiḥ guḍūcī kuṭajo vāsā kuṣmāṇḍaś ca śatāvarī
children.translated_text: except <s>viḍaṅga</s>, black pepper, molasses, grain, ghee, and honey. <s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, the two <s>sahacara</s>s, <s>śatapuṣpī</s>, and <s>prasāriṇī</s>
are always to be used moist; they are not to be doubled.

children.text: vāsā nimbapaṭolaketakībalā kuṣmāṇḍakendīvarī varṣābhūkuṭajāśvagandhasahitās tāḥ pūtigandhāmṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsā</s>, neem, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>, blue lotus, <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, and <s>aśvagandhā</s>, together with <s>pūtigandhā</s> and <s>amṛtā</s>,

children.text: māṃsaṃ nāgabalā sahacarapūgahiṅgvārdrake nityaśo grāhyas tat pala eva na dviguṇitāṃ ye cekṣujātāghanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: meat, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>sahacara</s>, areca nut, asafoetida, and fresh ginger should always be taken as only one <s>pala</s>, not doubled; likewise the solid products of sugarcane.

children.text: ekasya cauṣadher yogo yat tatra punar ucyate
children.translated_text: When a preparation involving a single medicinal substance is mentioned there again,
that substance is said by those who know the truth to be double by measure.

children.text: dravyābhāve dravyam anyad dviguṇaṃ vihitaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: When a substance is unavailable, another beneficial substance is prescribed in double quantity.

children.text: yogayuktaṃ yadā prāpyaṃ yuktitulyaṃ ca nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: When the substance suited to the formula is obtainable, one should add an amount equal according to proper reasoning.
For all great trees one should provide root-bark.
For creepers and small trees one should prescribe the whole plant.

children.text: sāras tu khadirādīnāṃ nimbādīnāṃ tvacaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: For khadira and the like, the heartwood is used; for neem and the like, the bark.

children.text: phalaṃ tu dāḍimādīnāṃ paṭolādeś chadas tathā ||
children.translated_text: For pomegranate and the like, the fruit is used; for <s>paṭola</s> and the like, the leaves.
In the absence of honey, old molasses is used; in the absence of milk, mung-bean preparation is used.

children.text: sitābhāve bhavet khaṇḍaḥ śālyabhāve ca ṣaṣṭikam ||
children.translated_text: In the absence of sugar, crystalline sugar is used; in the absence of rice, sixty-day rice is used.
In the absence of gold or silver, one should prepare it with iron.
In the absence of grapes, use <s>kāśmarya</s>; when pomegranate is lacking, use sour tree-fruit.

children.text: drave 'py anukte jalam atra deyaṃ kāle 'py anukte divasasya pūrvam
children.translated_text: When no liquid is specified, water is to be given here; when no time is specified, it is the first part of the day.

children.text: bhāge 'py anukte samatā vidhānam 'ṅge 'py anukte vihitaṃ tu mūlam ||
children.translated_text: When no proportion is specified, equality is the rule; when no part is specified, the root is prescribed.

children.text: cūrṇe snehe tathā lehe prāyaś candanāni ca
children.translated_text: In powders, oily preparations, and electuaries, sandalwoods are generally used.
In decoctions and applications, red sandalwood is generally employed.

children.text: lavaṇe saindhavaṃ dadyān mūtre gomūtram iṣyate
children.translated_text: For salt, one should give rock salt; for urine, cow urine is approved.
In preparations with milk and ghee, cow-derived milk and ghee alone are prescribed.
When no vessel is specified, use an earthen vessel; when no oil is specified, use sesame oil.

children.text: viśeṣo yatra noktaḥ syād eṣas tatra vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where no special rule has been stated, this is remembered as the rule there.
This measure has been stated for measures that are not specified.

children.text: karṣādau tu palaṃ yāvad dadyāt ṣoḍaśikaṃ jalam ||
children.translated_text: From <s>karṣa</s> and the like up to a <s>pala</s>, one should add sixteen times as much water.

children.text: tatas tu kuḍavo yāvat toyam aṣṭaguṇaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Then up to a <s>kuḍava</s>, the water should be eightfold.
Above that, up to a <s>prastha</s> and beyond, water should be at most fourfold.
For a soft substance, fourfold water is to be given; for a hard substance, it should be eightfold.
For something harder than that, sixteenfold water is recommended.

children.text: draveṇa yāvad vā dravyam ekībhūyārdratāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: As much liquid as will cause the substance to become unified and moist,
that much quantity is to be used by physicians in the procedure of levigation.
When dry substance has been taken and fresh juices are unavailable,
it should be cooked in eight times as much water, and the quarter that remains is taken.
Medicinal plants from anthills, sandy ground, marshland, cremation grounds, tracks,
and those pervaded by living creatures, fire, or frost, do not accomplish the desired medicinal work.
Medicinal plants born in anthills, wells, roads, under trees, temples, or cremation grounds,

children.text: jātā vidhināpihṛtā auṣadhyaḥ siddhidā na syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: even when gathered according to rule, do not grant success.
A body that is impaired by water, consumed by digestive fire, untimely, dry, and worm-eaten,

children.text: nyūnaṃ samadhikaṃ dravyaṃ na siddhidam iti jalpur bhiṣajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a substance that is deficient or excessive, physicians say, does not bring success.
Fruits, leaves, and the like are fit for one year; wood and stems for two years.

children.text: mūlaṃ trivarṣaṃ bījaṃ tu syāt saṃvatsarapañcakam
children.translated_text: Roots are fit for three years, but seeds for a period of five years.

children.text: niryāso daśamaṃ varṣaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ na praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: An exudation is fit up to the tenth year; beyond that it is not praised.

children.text: lehaṃ pāṇiṃ talaṃ tathaiva guṭikā cākṣapramāṇaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>leha</s> (lickable preparation) is a handful, likewise a palmful; a pill is the size of an akṣa, and powder,
the sages say, is the measure of a cat's foot; collyrium is the measure of a mung bean.
For the eyes, water is four drops; for the nostrils, six drops.

children.text: randhre pūrṇatamaṃ ca karṇayugale gaṇḍūṣamāsye rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the two ear openings it should be completely full; in the mouth, the liquid is a mouthful for gargling.
A paste should be of one karṣa measure; a mineral or mercurial medicine is only a guñjā in measure.

children.text: kaṣāyaḥ palaṃmātraṃ syād iti bhojamatam viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: A decoction should be one pala in measure: this they know as <s>Bhoja</s>'s opinion.

children.text: yāmaṃ kalkaṃ kaṣāyavīryam akhilaṃ cūrṇaṃ ca pakṣatrayaṃ ṣaṇmāsaṃ ghṛtalehayo sapurayor māsatrayaṃ modakaḥ
children.translated_text: A paste and the full potency of a decoction last for one yāma; powder lasts for three fortnights; ghee and lickable preparations, together with sapura, last six months; a sweet bolus lasts three months.

children.text: siddhānāṃ rasabhasmanāṃ suvipulaṃ vīryaṃ ca varṣatrayaṃ kiṃcid gandhavivarjitaṃ guṇakaraṃ tailaṃ purāṇaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: The potency of prepared rasas and ashes is very great for three years; old oil, if somewhat free from odor, is greatly beneficial.

children.text: kvāthaś ca kalkaś ca rasaś ca yāmaṃ yāmatrayaṃ modakavarticūrṇam
children.translated_text: A decoction, a paste, and fresh juice last for one yāma; boluses, wicks, and powders last for three yāmas.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsalehyaṃ ghṛtaguggulubhyām abdāt paraṃ tailakṛtaṃ ca vīryam ||
children.translated_text: A lickable lasts six months; ghee and guggulu preparations retain potency beyond a year; so too oil-made preparations.

children.text: śītaṃ jalaṃ jīryati yāmamātre yāmārdhake jīryati taptatoyam
children.translated_text: Cold water is digested in one yāma; hot water is digested in half a yāma.

children.text: kalkaś ca cūrṇaṃ ca ghaṭī tṛtīye kaṣāyakaṃ jīryati yāmamātre ||
children.translated_text: Paste and powder are digested in the third ghaṭī; a decoction is digested in one yāma.

children.text: yāmadvaye tu svarasā vasāś ca jīryanti te saptaghaṭīṣu sadyaḥ
children.translated_text: Fresh juices and fats are digested in two yāmas; those are digested quickly in seven ghaṭīs.

children.text: jīryanti lehyāny api pañcaghaṭyāṃ yāmatraye jīryati dugdhajātam ||
children.translated_text: Lickable preparations too are digested in five ghaṭīs; milk products are digested in three yāmas.

children.text: yāmadvaye jīryati vā ghṛtānnaṃ piṣṭaṃ tathā jīryati pañcayāme
children.translated_text: Food prepared with ghee is digested in two yāmas, while ground flour preparation is digested in five yāmas.

children.text: sārddhe triyāmā dadhi śuktam annaṃ māṃsaṃ tathā jīryati tāvad eva ||
children.translated_text: Curd, sour gruel, cooked rice, and meat are digested in three and a half yāmas, just so long.

children.text: annaṃ tadā jīryati pañcarātre kṣīraṃ tathā saptaniśīthinīṣu
children.translated_text: Then cooked food is digested in five nights, and milk likewise in seven nights.

children.text: khanetrarātrau dadhi jīrṇamāse māsārdhike jīryati dugdhasāram ||
children.translated_text: Curd is fully digested after many nights, and cream of milk is digested in half a month.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ gate māsi sujīrṇam āste māsadvaye jīryati māṃsam eva ca
children.translated_text: Ghee remains well digested when a month has passed, and meat itself is digested in two months.
In illnesses arising from the state of indigestion, what is beneficial and harmful in that condition must be considered.

children.text: dvibhāgaṃ pūrayed annaṃ toyaṃ bhāgaṃ prapūrayet
children.translated_text: One should fill two parts with food and fill one part with water.
For the movement of wind, one should leave the remaining part empty.
One should eat within a yāma; one should not exceed two yāmas.
Within one yāma the formation of <s>rasa</s> occurs; after two yāmas there is loss of strength.

children.text: athātaḥ svarasaḥ kalkaḥ kvāthaś ca himaphāṇṭakau
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, <s>svarasa</s> (fresh juice), <s>kalka</s> (paste), <s>kvātha</s> (decoction), <s>hima</s> (cold infusion), and <s>phāṇṭa</s> (hot infusion),
the <s>kaṣāya</s> (extractive preparation) is declared fivefold; its two subtypes are <s>yūṣa</s> (soup) and <s>mantha</s> (stirred drink).

children.text: vastraniṣpīḍitaṃ yat tu cūrṇitaṃ dviguṇe jale
children.translated_text: That which is squeezed through cloth after being powdered in twice as much water,

children.text: ahorātraṃ sthitaṃ vāpi svaraso dvividho mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or else left standing for a day and night, is considered a twofold <s>svarasa</s>.
Sugar, honey, jaggery, alkali, cumin, and salt,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ ca cūrṇādi kolamātraṃ rase kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: as well as ghee, oil, powder, and the like, should be put into the juice in a kola measure.

children.text: dravyam ādyaṃ śilāpiṣṭaṃ śuṣkaṃ vā sajalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The first substance, ground on a stone, may be dry or moistened with water.
A paste is made in the measure of a karṣa; honey and the rest should be added in double quantity.

children.text: sitā guḍaṃ samaṃ dadyāt dravād deyāś caturguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sugar and jaggery should be given in equal quantity; liquids should be given in fourfold quantity.
One pala of crushed substance should be put into sixteen palas of water.

children.text: śṛtaṃ tad dvipalaṃ grāhyaṃ kvātho niryūha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: When boiled, two palas of it should be taken; this is called <s>kvātha</s>, or <s>niryūha</s>.

children.text: kṣuṇṇaṃ dravyaṃ palaṃ samyak ṣaḍbhir nīrapalaiḥ plutam
children.translated_text: One pala of properly crushed substance, soaked in six palas of water,

children.text: viśoṣitaṃ himaḥ sa syāt tathā śītakaṣāyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and dried down, is <s>hima</s>; it is also a cold decoction.
One pala of properly crushed substance should be put into four times as much hot water,

children.text: kṣiptvā niṣpīḍya vastreṇa taddravo pāṇṭha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: then squeezed through cloth; that liquid is called <s>phāṇṭa</s>.
One pala of paste-drug, with dry ginger and long pepper each half a karṣa,

children.text: vāriprasthe ca vipacet taddravo yūṣa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: should be cooked in a prastha of water; that liquid is called <s>yūṣa</s>.
One pala of crushed substance should be put into four palas of cold water,

children.text: mṛtpātre manthayet samyak mantha ity abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and stirred thoroughly in an earthen vessel; it is called <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: kvāthaṃ caturguṇaṃ vāri kalkam aṣṭaguṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: For a decoction the water is four times as much; for a paste it is eight times as much.

children.text: kaṣāyaṃ ca daśaguṇaṃ pācanaṃ dvādaśam bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For a kaṣāya it is ten times as much, and for a digestive preparation it should be twelve times as much.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ piṣṭaṃ vastrapūtaṃ cūrṇaṃ tat parikīrtitam
children.translated_text: What is dried, ground, and strained through cloth is called powder.
That powder, in the measure of a karṣa, should be mixed with twice as much ghee and the like.
The liquid without grains is <s>maṇḍa</s>; <s>peyā</s> is accompanied by grains.
<s>Yavāgū</s> has many grains, and <s>vilepī</s> has sparse liquid.

children.text: annaṃ pañcaguṇe sādhyaṃ vilepī tu caturguṇe
children.translated_text: Rice should be cooked in five times as much water, but <s>vilepī</s> in four times as much.
<s>Maṇḍa</s> is made in four times as much, and <s>yavāgū</s> in six times as much water.
<s>Yūṣa</s>, according to <s>Śārṅgadhara</s>, is made in eighteen times as much water.

children.text: palaṃ kaṣāye dravaṃ syāt yavāgvāṃ ca tadardhakam
children.translated_text: In a decoction the liquid should be one pala; in <s>yavāgū</s> it is half of that.

children.text: pānīyeṣu tadarddhaṃ syād iti dravyasya niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In drinking waters it should be half of that again: this is the settled measure of the substance.

children.text: kvāthyamānaṃ tu yat toyaṃ niṣphenaṃ nirmalīkṛtam
children.translated_text: Water that is being boiled, freed of foam and made clear,

children.text: bhavaty ardhāvaśiṣṭaṃ ca tad uṣṇodakam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and becomes reduced to half its remainder, is called hot water.

children.text: dravyād aṣṭaguṇaṃ kṣīraṃ kṣīrāt toyaṃ caturguṇam
children.translated_text: Milk should be eight times the drug, and water four times the milk.
It should be brought down until only the milk remains; this is the rule in milk decoction.
Water and milk are each in eight parts, and honey is made the third component.

children.text: madhu śeṣe bhaved yāvat tāvat paktvāvatārayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be cooked and taken down when as much as the honey remains.
<s>Kāñjikā</s> is prescribed here by measure as one droṇa, with sour ferment.
Here, in the rule for śukta, there is one prastha of gruel-water, together with five āḍhakas.
There is one kuḍava of sour gruel, curd, one prastha of molasses, and sour radish.

children.text: palāny aṣṭau śodhitārdrāt palaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: There are eight palas of purified fresh ginger, and likewise sixteen palas.
Kaṇā, cumin, rock-salt, turmeric, and black pepper are each taken
in a quantity of two palas, infused in a vessel and kept for eight days in grain.
That śukta is ready when it is taken down and removed.
The four aromatics are also to be added, each with the measure of one karṣa.
The washing of the fragrant substances is done with water of the five pallavas,

children.text: śoṣaṇaṃ cāpi saṃskāro viśeṣaś cātra kathyate ||
children.translated_text: and drying too is the preparation; the special rule here is now stated.
The four āmalakas are precisely what is called triphalā.

children.text: māghe harītakī grāhyā phālgune ca vibhītakī
children.translated_text: Harītakī is to be taken in Māgha, vibhītakī in Phālguna,

children.text: caitre cāmalakī grāhyā triphalā saphalā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and āmalakī in Caitra; then triphalā will be fruitful.

children.text: harītakī pañcarasā ca recanī koṣṭhāmayaghnī lavaṇena varjitā
children.translated_text: Harītakī has five tastes, is purgative, destroys disorders of the bowels, and is devoid of salt.
It is rasāyana, removes eye disease, destroys skin disorders, and indeed carries the effect of the formulation.
It opens up the intellect, strength, and senses, and destroys pitta, kapha, and wind.
It is life-restoring among all rasāyanas, as Soma is among all plants.
After eating it is wholesome; before eating it is wholesome; eaten both before and after, it is wholesome and unwholesome.
When food is digested it is wholesome; when undigested it is wholesome; when both digested and undigested, it is wholesome and unwholesome.
Taken before and after food it causes vomiting; in the digested and undigested state it causes purgation.
Vibhītaka is pungent, bitter, astringent, hot, and removes kapha.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaḥ palitaghnaś ca vipāke madhuro laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: It benefits the eyes, destroys greying of hair, and in post-digestive effect is sweet and light.

children.text: tadvad āmalakam amlam uttamaṃ śītavīryaṃ kaphapittanāśanam
children.translated_text: Similarly āmalaka is sour, excellent, cold in potency, and destroys kapha and pitta.

children.text: keśyam akṣogadaghātīśītalaṃ vṛṣyam āśu vinihanti ṣaṇḍatām ||
children.translated_text: It benefits the hair, removes disease of the eyes, is cooling, aphrodisiac, and quickly destroys impotence.
Pippalī, black pepper, and dry ginger are called tryūṣaṇa, the three pungents.
Pippalī cures fever, is aphrodisiac, unctuous, hot, pungent, and bitter.
It kindles digestion and removes wind, dyspnea, cough, phlegm, and wasting.

children.text: maricaṃ laghu tiktarasaṃ kaṭukaṃ ghāti ca hṛdrogasaṃśamanam
children.translated_text: Black pepper is light, bitter in taste, pungent, destructive, and pacifies heart disease.
It removes worms and wind, produces relish, purifies the voice, and removes throat disorders.

children.text: śuṇṭhī snigdhā śothaśūlānilaghnī coṣṇā kaṭvī śleṣmadoṣān nihanti
children.translated_text: Dry ginger is unctuous, destroys swelling, pain, and wind, is hot and pungent, and destroys phlegmatic disorders.
It removes hiccup, cough, distension, abdominal obstruction, dyspnea, weak digestive fire, and disorders beginning with āma.
Svarjikā and yavaśūka are called the pair of alkalis.
The third alkali is ṭaṅkaṇa, which destroys abdominal tumors, urinary stones, and the like.
The three aromatics are cardamom, cinnamon bark, and leaf; the four aromatics include saffron.

children.text: madhuraṃ malinahṛt syāt tiktam īṣat kaṭūṣṇam
children.translated_text: They are sweet and remove impurity; they are bitter, slightly pungent, and hot.
They give strength, remove lack of appetite, are cold in potency, and so in post-digestive effect.
Cardamom destroys poison, poison-bite, anal piles, and obesity.
It removes pradarā, throat disorders, catarrh, dyspnea, and cough.
It is pungent, cold, destroys kapha and cough, and benefits the voice.
It pacifies seminal disorders and prameha, is light, and produces purity of the throat.
Patraka is light, bitter, hot, and removes poison, wind, and kapha.
It destroys disorders of the bladder, throat, and the three doṣas, and cleanses the mouth and head.

children.text: nāgakeśaram atīva śītalaṃ pittadāhaśamanaṃ ca tiktakam
children.translated_text: Nāgakeśara is extremely cooling, pacifies pitta and burning, and is bitter.
It removes blood disorders arising in the bladder and throat and kapha; it is somewhat hot, light in digestion, and aphrodisiac.
There are cumin, black cumin, and kaṇajīra as the third.

children.text: jīrakaḥ kaṭur udīrito himo dīpanaṃ kṛmiharo 'rśasāṃ hitaḥ
children.translated_text: Cumin is declared pungent and cold; it kindles digestion, destroys worms, and is beneficial in hemorrhoids.
It checks looseness, wind-pain, and diarrhea, and removes abdominal tumors, colic, and irregular fever.
They call camphor, musk, and saffron the triad beginning with camphor.
Camphor is sweet, somewhat bitter, pungent, and removes vomiting and burning.

children.text: śītapittaharaḥ karoti na kapha,ṛṣṭo nidāghe hito
children.translated_text: It removes śītapitta and does not produce kapha; when well used it is beneficial in summer.

children.text: dagdhāṅge śiśire ca pīnasagare pathyo 'lpa uṣṇaḥ kaṭuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a burned limb, in winter, and in the ocean of catarrh it is wholesome; in small quantity it is hot and pungent.
Rich in fragrance, destroying worms, removing kapha, and purifying the channels,
spreading delight in desire, removing fatigue, bitter, and greatly kindling the digestive fire,
removing pungent moisture and poison, itself somewhat pungent, auspicious, and beneficial as body perfume:

children.text: ity evaṃ kathitāś caturdaśa guṇāḥ kastūrikāyāḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus the fourteen qualities of musk have been stated.

children.text: yā gandhaḥ ketakīnāṃ harati parimalair varṇataḥ piṅgalābhā
children.translated_text: That fragrance which surpasses the fragrance of ketakī flowers, and which in color has a tawny appearance,

children.text: svāde tiktā kaṭvī laghur atha tulitā marditā cikkaṇā syāt ||
children.translated_text: which in taste is bitter and pungent, light when weighed, and, when rubbed, becomes smooth,

children.text: kṣiptāgnau bhasma na syāc cimicimi kurute carmagandhā hutāśe
children.translated_text: which, when thrown into fire, does not become ash but crackles, and gives a leathery smell in the flame,

children.text: sā śuddhā śobhanāsyā varamṛgatanujā rājayogyā prasiddhā ||
children.translated_text: that pure, excellent musk from the body of the noble deer is known as fit for kings.

children.text: karatalajalamadhye sthāpayitvā muhūrtaṃ punar api yadi paśyed daṇḍamātraṃ nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: Having placed it for a moment in water in the palm of the hand, if one looks again, observing it for the length of a staff,

children.text: yadi bhavati ca raktaṃ tajjalaṃ pītavarṇaṃ na bhavati mṛganābhiḥ kṛtrimo 'sau vikāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: if that water becomes red and not yellow in color, that mṛganābhi is not genuine; it is an artificial alteration.
Saffron is fragrant, bitter, pungent and hot, and destroys cough, pitta, kapha, and throat pain.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ śūlaviṣadoṣaharaṃ tadrocanaṃ tu tanukāntikaraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It removes upward pain and poison disorders; it gives relish and produces delicacy and beauty of the body.

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ saindhavaṃ ca viḍam audbhidam eva ca
children.translated_text: Sauvarcala, saindhava, viḍa, and audbhida,

children.text: sāmudreṇa sahaitāni pañca syur lavaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: together with sea salt, are the five salts.

children.text: teṣu mukhyaṃ saindhavaṃ syāt sarvabhāveṣu kṣepayet ||
children.translated_text: Among them saindhava is the chief and should be added in all preparations.

children.text: sindhūdbhavaṃ netrarujāpahaṃ ca saṃdīpanīyaṃ rucivṛṣyam uktam
children.translated_text: Rock-salt is said to arise from Sindhu, remove eye diseases, kindle digestion, produce relish, and be aphrodisiac.

children.text: pūtaṃ tridoṣopaśamaṃ karoti viḍbandhanaṃ svādurasaṃ vraṇaghnam ||
children.translated_text: When purified, it pacifies the three doṣas, relieves fecal obstruction, has a sweet taste, and heals wounds.
<s>Kākolī</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, likewise

children.text: medaś cāpi mahāmedo jīvantī madhukaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>medā</s>, <s>mahāmedā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>:
<s>mudgaparṇī</s> and <s>māṣaparṇī</s>; this is the <s>jīvanīya</s> group.
It promotes breast milk, is nourishing, aphrodisiac, promotes conception, and is heavy.

children.text: dvau medau dvau ca kākolyau jīvakarṣabhakau tathā
children.translated_text: The two <s>medā</s>s, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>,
together with <s>ṛddhi</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s>, are the eightfold group; its qualities are equal to the <s>jīvanīya</s> group.
When <s>medā</s> is absent, <s>aśvagandhā</s> may be used; for <s>mahāmedā</s>, <s>sārivā</s>.

children.text: ṛddhyabhāve balā grāhyā vṛddhau tv atibalā tathā ||
children.translated_text: When <s>ṛddhi</s> is absent, <s>balā</s> should be taken; for <s>vṛddhi</s>, likewise <s>atibalā</s>.
When the pair of <s>kākolī</s>s is absent, one should put in <s>śatāvarī</s>.
When <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s> are absent, <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>vaṃśalocana</s> are used.
In a disorder of wind it is very hot, in phlegm hot, and in bile and blood very cooling.

children.text: saṃsarge tat samoṣṇaṃ syāt sannipāte tv aśītalam ||
children.translated_text: In combined disorders it should have that same degree of heat; but in a triple-doṣa condition it should not be cold.
By day, because the doṣas are slight, half a <s>prasṛta</s> of decoction is proper.

children.text: rātrau śītāṃśukiraṇair dhātūn puṣyanti te malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At night, under the rays of the moon, those impurities nourish the bodily constituents.
Because the doṣas are abundant at night, drinking a full <s>prasṛta</s> is beneficial.

children.text: tṛṣite gaṇḍūṣatoyasya pāne kvātheṣv ayaṃ kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When one is thirsty, drinking water for gargling: this is the procedure in decoctions.
If the essence of the bodily constituent has not been purified, it remains until the end of life; there is no doubt.
Indeed all the bodily constituents, though dead, become like nectar.

children.text: antaḥ sunīlo bahir ujjvalo yo madhyāhnasūryapratimaprakāśaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury that is dark blue within, bright outside, and has a brilliance like the midday sun,

children.text: śasto 'tha dhūmraḥ paripāṇḍuraś ca sūto na yojyo rasakarmasiddhau ||
children.translated_text: is praised; but smoky or very pale mercury should not be used for successful rasa work.
In a mortar, with powders of turmeric and brick-dust, each one sixteenth of the mercury and other substances,
one should triturate it with citron juice; then it becomes purified.
One should also triturate mercury with aloe and turmeric powder,

children.text: pātayet pātanayantre samyak śuddho raso bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and distill it in a distillation apparatus; the rasa becomes properly purified.

children.text: nāgavaṅgamalo vahniś cāñcalyaṃ ca viṣaṃ giriḥ
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, impurity, fire, mobility, poison, mountain-mineral,

children.text: atyagniś cāṣṭadoṣāś ca nisargāt pārade sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and excessive fire: these eight defects are naturally present in mercury.

children.text: saurṇai niśeṣṭakā dhūmra jambīrāmbubhir ā dinam
children.translated_text: Triturated for a day with gold-colored turmeric, brick-powder, smoke-colored material, and citron water,

children.text: marditaḥ kāṃjikair dhauto nāgadoṣaṃ rasas tyajet ||
children.translated_text: and washed with sour gruel, mercury abandons the defect of lead.
With powder of <s>viśālā</s> and <s>aṅkoṭha</s> it releases the defect of tin.
<s>Rājavṛkṣa</s> destroys impurity, and <s>citraka</s> the defect of fire.
Black <s>dhustūra</s> removes mobility, and <s>triphala</s> destroys poison.

children.text: kaṭutrayaṃ giriṃ hanti atyagniṃ ca trikaṇṭakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The three pungents destroy the mountain-mineral defect, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s> excessive fire.
For each defect, the wise man should use the appropriate powder, with another ingredient, in the measure of one <s>kalā</s> part,
and wash it in an earthen vessel with warmed sour gruel that has been lifted off the fire.
Thus purified, mercury is free from the seven coverings.
Freed from the eight defects and free from the seven coverings,

children.text: viśuddho jāyate sūtaḥ tataḥ karmaṇi yajayet ||
children.translated_text: mercury becomes purified; then one should employ it in procedures.
Combined with one quarter part of sulfur and pomegranate sour water,
rasa is killed with a lump of the root of barren <s>karkoṭikā</s>.
Castor root, root of <s>vaḍavāgni</s>, <s>dhustūra</s> root, and a quantity of salt:

children.text: saṃghaṭṭayet bhāṇḍayugme rasas tu bhasmibhavec candrasamānakāntiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should rub them together between two vessels, and the rasa becomes ash, with a lustre like the moon.
Mercury should be triturated for three days with the root-like fiber of white <s>aṅkoṭha</s>.
When heated in a sealed crucible, mercury attains the state of ash.
Two <s>pala</s>s of purified mercury and half as much purified sulfur

children.text: kanyānīreṇa saṃmardya radhvā tu bhūdhare pacet
children.translated_text: should be triturated with the water of <s>kanyā</s>; after rubbing, one should cook it in a closed earthen apparatus.
It is killed, without doubt; one should use it in all diseases.
A lump made from white <s>aṅkoṭha</s> and <s>śirīṣa</s> water, in a mortar for three days,
when triturated and placed in a sealed crucible, causes mercury to attain the state of ash.
Mercury destroys all diseases; having the six tastes, it carries off all diseases.
It is the king of formulations made of the five elements, making the body like iron and granting success.
Mercury destroys worms and skin disease, benefits the eyes, and is a rejuvenative.
It is a carrier of formulations, very potent, and prevents old age and death.

children.text: tāre guṇāśīti tadarddhakānte vaṃge catuṣṣaṣṭi raje tadarddham
children.translated_text: In silver there are eighty qualities, in beautiful copper half of that; in tin sixty-four, in calx half of that.

children.text: svarṇe sahasraṃ gagane śatekaṃ vajre guṇākoṭiś cānanta sūte ||
children.translated_text: In gold there are a thousand, in mica a hundred and one; in diamond there are ten million qualities, and in mercury endless ones.
One should place one hundred <s>pala</s>s of <s>harabīja</s> in the middle of the mortar,
or else half of that, half of that again, or half of that again.

children.text: pāradaṃ palamātraṃ syād anyūnaṃ kurute bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The physician should use mercury in the measure of one <s>pala</s>, making it not deficient.
With utterances of the <s>Aghora</s> mantra he should worship it sixteenfold.

children.text: khallamadhye tataḥ sthāpya śodhayec ca bhiṣagvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after placing it in the middle of the mortar, the excellent physician should purify it.
Mixed with turmeric powder, he should triturate it for two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s.
Mixed with household soot, he should expose it to sunlight.
Having put it inside a white cloth, the wise man should impregnate it with rasa.

children.text: śikhaṇḍī pūtikāṣṭhaṃ ca eṣikā phaṇī vallikā
children.translated_text: <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>, rotten wood, <s>eṣikā</s>, <s>phaṇī</s>, and <s>vallikā</s>,
<s>kakkola</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>tuṇḍī</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: aṅkolaṃ rājavṛkṣaś ca kāñcanasya dravair api
children.translated_text: <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, and also the fluids of <s>kāñcana</s>,
and the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and <s>varṣābhū</s>: having added these, one should triturate it.

children.text: nirdravaṃ marditaḥ patrarasaiḥ śuddhi bhaved rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it has been triturated until dry with the juices of leaves, the rasa becomes purified.
<s>Harabīja</s>, rasa, sūta, pārada, capala, and amṛta:
these are names of mercury; one should use it in all diseases.
This sulfur, placed in the front half of a vessel with milk, becomes purified by the tortoise heating process.

children.text: kṣudrīkṛtaḥ sājya caṭusthito 'gnau dravīkṛto dugdhanipātito vā ||
children.translated_text: Or, when reduced to small pieces, placed with ghee in a ladle, melted over fire, and dropped into milk,
purified sulfur removes diseases; it removes skin disease, death, and fever.

children.text: agnikārī mahān uṣṇo vīryavṛddhiṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: It kindles digestion, is greatly hot, and increases virility.

children.text: palamātraṃ rasaṃ śuddhaṃ tāvanmānaṃ ca gandhakam
children.translated_text: One should take a pala measure of purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury), and the same measure of sulfur,
and, after making them into <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulfide mixture) according to rule, with water from shoots of the banyan tree,
after giving three rounds of levigation, one should place it in a glass bottle.

children.text: kramād agniṃ tato dadyād bhiṣag yāmacatuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: Then the physician should apply fire gradually for four <s>yāmas</s>.
There arises <s>rasasindūra</s>, resembling the young red sun;
according to the particular accompanying vehicle, it produces various beneficial effects.
